title: Erysipelas (bright red skin infection)

items: Erysipelas is a superficial skin infection with a sharp, raised edge.
It is usually caused by a strep germ.
A bright red, raised, firm patch with a clear, raised border.
Fever, chills, and feeling unwell. Often on the legs or face.
Blood cultures if you are unwell.
Your doctor will choose antibiotics based on how unwell you are.
Ask your doctor about the course length.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Raise the affected limb, and rest.
Mark the edge of the redness to see if it spreads.
See your doctor if the redness spreads or you are not better after a few days.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Redness spreading fast, or dark or blistered skin
Fever with feeling faint or confused
Severe pain or swelling that is getting worse
